blocks.text: Intro

Solo slightly detuned upright piano. Four jaunty notes, the last one suspiciously wrong. A pause. Upright bass enters with a confident walking line. Brushed snare joins. Lopsided vaudeville two-step, moderate tempo.
Verse 1
Male baritone, wry, talk-sung, cheerful enough to be suspicious

Well, the world's gone and changed the rules again
They've moved the finish line
The ladder's missing half its rungs
But the view up here's just fine

They tell me there's a future
And they tell me there's a plan
I haven't seen the paperwork
But I'm doing what I can
Pre-Chorus
Bass walks upward. Piano chases with playful, slightly dissonant flourishes. Vocal leans forward as if sharing a secret.

There's a cliff around the corner
There's a drop beneath the floor
But there's something rather lovely
We haven't tried before
Chorus
Melody becomes unexpectedly clear and memorable. Instruments briefly agree on the downbeat. Sincere without becoming sentimental.

We haven't heard from you yet
Haven't seen what you might do
There's a world of little wonders
That could only come from you

I can't promise you a landing
I can't tell you where we'll get
But the world's not done surprising us
We haven't heard from you yet
Instrumental Turnaround
Eight bars. Walking bass holds steady while the detuned piano trips through playful chromatic runs. A clarinet wanders in, offers an unsolicited opinion, and wanders back out.
Verse 2
More rhythmic and mischievous. Singer enjoys the absurdity.

There's a fellow at the arcade
Who's discovered how to win
While the others throw their quarters
He just reaches right on in

Now he's standing at the counter
With a mountain of cheap toys
And the children who've been practicing
Are making quite a noise
Pre-Chorus
Dry rimshot. Piano drops out for the first two lines, leaving bass and voice.

Well, maybe they've got reason
To be angry at the game
But the fellow found another way
And the prizes spend the same
Chorus
Slightly fuller. Clarinet quietly shadows the melody, occasionally landing on a questionable note.

We haven't heard from you yet
Haven't seen what you might do
There's a world of little wonders
That could only come from you

I can't promise you a landing
I can't tell you where we'll get
But the world's not done surprising us
We haven't heard from you yet
Bridge
Arrangement thins. Bass continues walking, softer now. Piano plays sparse single notes. Vocal loses its theatrical confidence without becoming sad.

A young woman asked me once
What hope she ought to keep
I gave her all my clever words
And lost a little sleep

I still think about that question
And the answer that I gave
I'd like to say I've found a better one
But I haven't, I'm afraid
Brief instrumental pause
Piano plays a tentative descending phrase. Bass stops for the first time.
Bridge continuation
Voice nearly spoken, direct and intimate.

I don't know what the world will want
Or what it'll let you keep
But I'd hate to think the things you'll make
Are things we'll never see
Build
Bass returns, picking up the walk exactly where it left off. Piano answers with a bright, crooked flourish. Brushes begin pushing forward.

So pull a chair up to the table
Make a mess and make a sound
There's no telling what we're missing
Till you put your something down
Final Chorus
Buoyant, not bombastic. The ensemble plays with exuberant imperfections. Clarinet circles the vocal. No choir, no grand swell.

We haven't heard from you yet
Haven't seen what you might do
There's a world of little wonders
That could only come from you

I can't promise you a landing
I can't tell you where we'll get
But the world's not done surprising us
We haven't heard from you yet
Outro
Instruments gradually peel away. Singer returns to amused, conversational delivery.

Make the thing
Make it wrong
Tear it up
And carry on

Take a chance
And take a breath
There's a little daylight left
Bass walks alone for four bars, approaching what sounds like a final cadence. Stops abruptly.
Spoken
Dry, warmly amused
Well, go on then.
One questionable piano note.
We're listening.
End
No resolution. No reverb tail.

notebook.style: Crooked vaudeville hymn, mischievous theatrical folk-jazz, lopsided 4/4 two-step, moderate brisk tempo, vintage acoustic ensemble, Slightly detuned upright piano plays jaunty chromatic figures, unexpected wrong notes, playful ragtime flourishes, Confident walking upright bass anchors everything, unwavering even as the arrangement teeters, Dry brushed snare, occasional rimshots, wandering clarinet with humorous countermelodies, Weathered male baritone, intimate talk-sung delivery, sly conversational phrasing, dry wit, expressive pauses, occasional melodic warmth, Charming and self-assured despite obvious uncertainty, Verses rhythmically playful, chorus surprisingly plainspoken and sincere, never sentimental, Bridge strips back to bass and sparse piano, briefly vulnerable, Final chorus buoyant but restrained, Imperfect live-room recording, analog warmth, natural dynamics, theatrical timing, No choir, no synths, no cinematic swells, no glossy production, Ends on an unresolved piano note
